title: Canonical map from the special-chart polynomial algebra
statement: Let R, Cbar, pi and arbitrary polynomial data d have the types in [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-lift-preparation], without assuming Prepared. Put C0=Cbar/(pi Cbar) and D0=D/(pi D), using the explicitly defined lifting quotient D. Suppose c:Cbar to D0 is an R-algebra map and cmod:C0 to D0 is a ring map whose composite with the quotient map is c. Fix k. Set a0 to the class of epsilon(reduced(a_k)) in C0 and t=c(epsilon(reduced(a_k))). The canonical C0-algebra map from C0[1/a0][Z_j:j in E_k] to D0[1/t] is coefficient localization of cmod, followed by polynomial evaluation sending Z_j to the class of the auxiliary variable z_j. Localization uses [lem-weil-pbc-localization-away-universal-property] and evaluation uses [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. No data are chosen from an unproved existence theorem.

source.place: Stacks Project, Tag 07CP, displayed calculation modulo pi and comparison of chart coefficients; read online at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07CP on 2026-10-13.

proof.text: The identity cmod composed with the quotient map equals c identifies the image of a0 with t. Its image in D0[1/t] is therefore a unit, proved by popescu_special_chart_coefficient_isUnit.

Lift the coefficient map through localization by IsLocalization.Away.liftAlgHom, and evaluate the free variables by MvPolynomial.aevalTower. The auxiliary variables are the explicit classes through the defining quotient, ULift and reduction by pi.
